blocks: I’ve never talked to anyone. I’m used to handling things on my own. Aren’t people who go to therapy weak?
Not at all. I see asking for help as a sign of awareness and courage, not weakness. I believe everyone needs support at different points in life.
In my work with you, I help you explore your strengths and understand how to use them to ease the challenges you are carrying.
What’s the difference between talking to you or my best friend or family?

The difference lies in my professional training, clinical expertise, and ability to guide meaningful change. Therapy is not simply a space to vent, it is a structured process led by a trained mental health professional who helps you better understand your thoughts, emotions, and patterns. I help you approach your situation from new perspectives, develop practical skills, and gain deeper self-awareness. I listen without judgment or expectations, while also guiding you in ways that support real, lasting progress. I provide a fully confidential space where you can speak openly without concern about others knowing your personal experiences. While friends and family can offer support, those relationships can sometimes become emotionally complicated, especially when difficult topics are involved. Therapy provides a neutral, consistent space focused entirely on your growth, without placing strain on your personal relationships.
Why shouldn’t I just take medication?

Medication can be effective, but it is not always a complete solution on its own. In many cases, it works best alongside therapy. I help you explore and understand the challenges you are experiencing, while also building on your strengths to support you in achieving your personal goals.
How does it work? What do I have to do in sessions?
Because each person has different concerns and goals for counseling, the process varies from person to person. I tailor my therapeutic approach to your specific needs.

Unfortunately, this is not something I can define in a general FAQ. Everyone’s circumstances are unique, and the length of time therapy takes depends on your goals, your commitment, and the factors that bring you to counseling in the first place.
I want to get the most out of therapy. What can I do to help?
I am glad you are committed to getting the most out of your sessions. Your active participation and willingness to engage in the process play an important role in your progress.

I’m Dr. Anna, a licensed psychologist with over 13 years of clinical experience. My training spans both California and Florida, where I developed a strong foundation in therapeutic care and comprehensive neuropsychological assessment for adolescents and adults. Presently I work in 40+ states, which allows my busy clients to see me during work trips, time off from college, or continue care after relocation.

Today, my work is highly specialized. I focus primarily on supporting teen girls and women navigating burnout—most often those with ADHD and other forms of neurodivergence. Neurodivergence is not just an area of interest in my practice; it is the core of it. I provide in-depth neuropsychological evaluations alongside targeted therapeutic work, including emotional regulation, relationship dynamics, and practical, skill-based coaching for organization and executive functioning.

My approach is holistic and integrative. I consider the full context of each individual’s life, including the intersection of mental health with physical and functional health. This often includes insights related to ADHD in women, autoimmune conditions, and other systemic factors that are frequently overlooked.

I believe meaningful care requires more than addressing isolated behaviors. Together, we look at the whole picture—so that the work we do is not only effective, but sustainable and deeply aligned with who you are.

I believe meaningful change happens through insight, connection, and skill-building. Therapy is not about fixing you — it’s about understanding patterns, strengthening relationships, and learning how to work with your mind rather than against it.
